items.titleTr: UK government set to publish new treaties agreed with EU
items.summaryTr: The BBC understands the treaties contain a 10-year termination clause to reimburse costs of any need to rebuild border checks infrastructure.
items.articleText: UK government set to publish new treaties agreed with EU - Published The government and the EU is set to publish the texts of two treaties on Thursday afternoon that were agreed last week as part of a new deal with the EU, as well as the UK legislation to enact the bulk of the deal. The BBC understands the treaties contain a 10-year termination clause that would mean if one party ended the agreement in that time they would have to pay to rebuild border checks infrastructure, which will be significantly scaled back as part of the new deal. That means that if a future government or the EU ended the deal, they would have to pay potentially significant costs to re-establish border controls. Opposition leader Kemi Badenoch and Reform UK's Nigel Farage have suggested they would refuse to pay. The Brexit reset deal has already sparked debate about its benefits, its costs, and a wider discussion on the long-term UK-EU relationship. The deal covers British food exports, emissions trading and a youth experience scheme. Two of the three legal texts will be released on Thursday, covering the food trade and emissions trading scheme deals, alongside the government's cost-cutting bill to enact the deal. The treaties will also have an impact on the UK aviation and maritime industries in terms of their alignment with EU emissions schemes. New assessments of the impact of the deal on different sectors and regions of the country are also expected. - EU offers UK fresh deal on 'Made in Europe' scheme - Published10 hours ago - Badenoch challenges Burnham over university fees for EU students - Published10 hours ago - Farage helps launch new campaign against the UK rejoining the EU - Published8 hours ago Under the deal, food exporters will be significant beneficiaries from the scrapping of considerable red tape and checks, and dismantling of border facilities. An internal analysis forecasts a 16% boost to agricultural exports. The industry and government hope the reduction in costs for food producers and sellers will be passed on to customers, but there may be no clear visible impact at the checkout. Privately, industry insiders told the BBC earlier this week that there are too many moving parts in the world economy, especially given the energy price shock resulting from war in the Middle East. Regarding the fine detail in the text of one of the treaties relating to the 10-year termination clause, European affairs minister Hamish Falconer said: "The Cutting Costs Bill allows us to implement two major trade agreements." "It allows us to eliminate paperwork for our food and drink traders, protect billions of pounds worth of British exports from carbon taxes, and make doing business with our largest trading partner cheaper and easier." The BBC also understands that full details of a plan to link British and EU emissions trading schemes will see more of the UK aviation and maritime industries covered. The treaty text will also contain the fine detail of how the UK will observe, shape but not vote on relevant EU rules. Plans to use secondary legislation, including granting direct so-called "Henry VIII powers" to ministers to align UK and EU laws will also be detailed in the legislation. Outlining the agreement with the EU to MPs earlier this week, the prime minister said new agreements with the EU are "pragmatic" and "not a prelude to anything". Andy Burnham also said it would be "unthinkable" for the UK to rejoin the bloc without a referendum. Several former prime ministers have urged him not to reopen the Brexit debate. Burnham said they are "stuck in the past" and later claimed there would be "no banging on about Europe" from Labour. Badenoch said Burnham has "oversold" the deal and was "trying to take Britain back to 2015".

items.title: As foreign troops withdraw from Somalia, could al-Shabab take over?
items.summary: Somalia relies heavily on foreign funding and military support for its very survival.

items.titleTr: As foreign troops withdraw from Somalia, could al-Shabab take over?
items.summaryTr: Somalia relies heavily on foreign funding and military support for its very survival.
items.articleText: As foreign troops withdraw from Somalia, could al-Shabab take over? - Published Somalia is facing a fresh test of its stability as foreign troops begin withdrawing, funding for its security forces comes under pressure and a bitter political dispute threatens to derail plans for the country's first direct democratic elections in decades. The combination of challenges has raised questions about whether the government can defend itself against Islamist militant group al-Shabab while managing growing divisions among political factions. Some analysts fear the situation could embolden al-Shabab, which is affiliated with al-Qaeda, and potentially allow it to seize control of the capital, Mogadishu. The group already controls large parts of the country despite the presence of about 12,000 African Union (AU) troops supporting the government. The withdrawal of foreign forces, alongside the activities of clan-based militias aligned with rival political factions, has heightened concerns about the government's ability to maintain control. Ugandan troops, who make up the largest contingent of the AU force, began withdrawing last month, with the country expected to complete its withdrawal by next year. Ethiopia, another major contributor to the AU mission, is also reportedly planning to withdraw about 3,000 troops. The country has 2,500 troops authorised under the AU mission and roughly 5,000 under a bilateral agreement with Somalia. It is not clear whether the reported withdrawals would be from the AU contingent, the bilateral force, or both. The US, which had earlier announced cuts to funding for the UN Support Office in Somalia (UNSOS) has since said it is extending it for a year. Washington contributes about a quarter of $500m UNSOS's annual budget, which supports Somali security forces, AU missions and individual troop-contributing nations. With military support uncertain and the government facing mounting political challenges, analysts question whether Somalia's security forces are ready to stand on their own. The concerns were heightened recently when al-Shabab claimed to have killed hundreds of elite Somali soldiers in an attack. The government acknowledged the attack but did not disclose the number of casualties. Abdisalam Guleid, a former deputy director of Somalia's National Security Agency, told the BBC the security situation was increasingly precarious. He warned that the withdrawal of foreign troops could leave Mogadishu vulnerable to a takeover similar to that of Afghanistan by the Taliban in 2021, following the withdrawal of US and Nato forces. "I don't think Mogadishu will be able to defend itself. The Taliban style [takeover]… that's the most likely scenario I can envision now," he said. The Taliban took over control of Afghanistan between 6-15 August 2021 in a rapid offensive, following the withdrawal of US and NATO forces. Such a scenario has played out in Somalia in the past, Guleid explains. - Why is Uganda fighting in 'hellish' Somalia? - Published15 March 2012 Somalia has experienced the collapse of central authority before. In the early 1990s, clan-based rebel groups advanced on Mogadishu from several fronts, forcing then-President Mohamed Siad Barre from power. His overthrow triggered a devastating civil war and a prolonged humanitarian crisis. The collapse of state institutions subsequently created conditions in which Islamist militant groups, including al-Shabab, were able to expand their influence. Guleid says Ugandan troops have been central to preventing a similar collapse since their first deployment to Somalia in 2007. They played a key role in driving al-Shabab out of Mogadishu and other major towns, while protecting strategic installations, including the airport, seaport, government institutions and diplomatic missions. Troops from Burundi, Djibouti, Kenya, Sierra Leone and Ethiopia later joined the AU mission, while countries including Turkey and the US maintained separate military deployments and provided training and equipment to Somali forces. But Guleid argues that years of international assistance have not translated into sufficient military independence for the Somali government. He says the authorities have become so reliant on foreign protection that they have neglected to adequately prepare their own forces to take over. Somalia's Information Minister Abdifatah Qasim Mohamud rejected suggestions that the country would be unable to cope with the withdrawals. He told the BBC that Somali troops had already taken over some positions vacated by Ugandan forces and were prepared to assume greater responsibility for the country's security. He said Somalia could not depend indefinitely on foreign troops for its protection. "I believe there is no reason for concern over this issue. There will be no change in the country's security situation or in the areas they have vacated," he said. President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud has also been seeking continued international backing. During a visit to Uganda on 23 November, he and President Yoweri Museveni called on the international community to continue supporting Somalia to consolidate security gains. Not everyone believes the withdrawal will necessarily result in a security collapse. Ugandan security analyst Freddie David Egesa argues that years of international military support have helped Somalia establish the institutions needed to take greater responsibility for its security. He says the withdrawal will provide an opportunity to assess how much progress has been made. It will also force Somalia's political leaders to put aside their differences and take greater responsibility for the country's future, he adds. But other analysts warn that the timing could hardly be worse. Omar Mahmood, an analyst at the International Crisis Group, says Somali forces are under considerable pressure as they fight al-Shabab while attempting to take over positions previously held by foreign troops. This is a major undertaking for an army that is still developing, he says. The military is also facing pressure in the Bay region of the South-West state, where forces loyal to ousted regional President Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed have been fighting the federal government. The withdrawal of Ugandan troops from the Lower Shabelle region could create further security challenges, Mahmood adds. Mahmood further points to the long-delayed elections, which need to be secured, as another issue compounding the security situation. Somalia has been attempting to move away from an indirect electoral system in which clan elders select lawmakers, who then elect the president, towards a system of direct voting. Beyond the military situation, Mahmood says, the government must also resolve a growing political dispute over the timing and format of the country's elections. But the proposed changes have divided the government and opposition, with disagreements over how the elections should be conducted. The dispute escalated this year after Mohamud pushed through constitutional amendments extending the presidential term from four to five years, effectively delaying the next elections until 2027. This month, the Supreme Court ruled against the extension, ordering political leaders to agree on an electoral roadmap within 30 days and to hold elections within three months. A day before the ruling, Mohamud dismissed Chief Justice Baashe Yusuf Ahmed. He and other judges in the case have filed a suit against Somalia over the dismissals at the East African regional court in Tanzania. The Somali government has since rejected the Supreme Court's decision, with its implementation now uncertain. Mahmood says the political and security crises are closely connected, with the absence of consensus over the elections making it harder for the government to focus on the fight against al-Shabab. Guleid also warns that the threat to Somalia's stability comes not only from the militant group but from clan-based militias increasingly challenging the federal government. "Today, we have clan loyalists fighting alongside al-Shabab against the federal government," he said. He added the country's leadership appears unable to anticipate the scale of the challenges ahead. Who will fill the gap left by foreign partners? Somalia's security challenges are compounded by its heavy dependence on international financial support. Latest data from its finance ministry shows that donor grants amounting to $878.8m accounts for two-thirds of its planned $1.36bn budget in 2026. Despite that, the ministry said it had only received about $314m of grants in the first nine months of the year, equivalent to 35% the expected annual aid. Mahmood believes that although some international military support is declining, other partners could help bridge the gap through bilateral agreements and continued assistance. But Guleid is sceptical that countries such as Turkey, Qatar and Egypt could quickly replace the military and financial contributions of Uganda and the US. He argues that Somalia's dependence on external support makes it particularly vulnerable when international partners change their priorities. That dependence has also contributed to increasingly strained relations with some foreign governments. Somalia has accused the United Arab Emirates of funding armed groups and undermining its sovereignty, in the latest dispute involving an external power with significant security and economic interests in the country. The UAE has rejected the criticism and hit back at the Somali leader, describing him as an "outgoing president" in reference to the dispute over his presidential mandate. The two countries formally severed ties earlier this year, although the UAE has long been an important security and economic partner in Somalia. The dispute illustrates the difficult relationship Somalia has with foreign partners on whom it relies for security, funding and political support. For Egesa, the withdrawal of foreign troops could ultimately provide an opportunity for Somalia to demonstrate how much progress it has made in rebuilding its security institutions. He believes the staggered departure of troops will allow Somali forces to assume responsibility gradually, while also forcing rival political factions to work together. But Guleid remains far less optimistic. He argues that unless Somalia addresses its military weaknesses, political divisions and growing influence of armed groups, it risks losing the security gains made. For now, it faces the difficult task of fighting an entrenched insurgency, managing rival political interests and preparing for a contentious electoral process, all while some of military partners are preparing to leave. Whether Somalia can withstand these pressures without renewed instability remains an open question. items.summary: AI is driving a massive wave of mathematical breakthroughs which could have implications for cryptography.

items.titleTr: AI labs likely sitting on cryptography ‘bombshells,’ computer scientist says
items.summaryTr: AI is driving a massive wave of mathematical breakthroughs which could have implications for cryptography.
items.articleText: AI labs likely sitting on cryptography ‘bombshells,’ computer scientist says AI is driving a massive wave of mathematical breakthroughs which could have implications for cryptography. Theoretical computer scientist Scott Aaronson says leading AI laboratories are likely sitting on undisclosed breakthroughs in cryptography. In a blog post on Wednesday, Aaronson, a former OpenAI researcher and professor at The University of Texas at Austin, warned that algorithms emerging from AI-driven mathematical advances will eventually break currently deployed cryptosystems. “I’m virtually certain, from multiple reliable sources, that the AI labs are now sitting on one or more bombshells in that area,” Aaronson said. “However, until I either see details or hear directly from someone at a lab, I feel much, much less confident about the specific nature of those bombshells.” The remarks add to concerns that AI’s accelerating mathematical capabilities could eventually undermine the cryptography used to secure crypto wallets and blockchain transactions. Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin and researcher Justin Drake raised those concerns in October. AI tackles longstanding mathematical problems Recent weeks have illustrated the pace at which AI has been able to overcome previously unsolvable math problems. On Friday, Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge released an AI-assisted proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, one of the most famous unsolved problems in mathematics. Alpöge developed it with an unreleased version of Claude over roughly six weeks, spanning 17 million lines of Lean code. The proof was later verified as correct by Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative. Days later, both Anthropic and OpenAI released proofs of the VP versus VNP conjecture, described as an algebraic cousin of P versus NP, another major unsolved problem in theoretical computer science. In October, OpenAI released 722 AI-generated math manuscripts covering 372 problem areas on GitHub, which has since been nicknamed the “mathocalypse.” “This past week — is very much like I would’ve always imagined the beginning of an AI singularity to look and feel like,” said Aaronson. Related: AI poses greater threat to Bitcoin than quantum computing, Swan founder says One of the rumors, according to Aaronson, is that one or both of the AI labs have solved “Factoring in P,” referring to a polynomial-time factoring algorithm — a breakthrough that could threaten RSA cryptography. AI commentator Andrew Curran and Carnegie Mellon University machine learning researcher Aran Nayebi also said they had heard similar rumors. Aaronson, however, declined to offer any insight on the idea that ECDSA, a digital signature scheme used by Bitcoin, had been broken. “Crucially, don’t want the cryptography part of the story to overshadow the intellectual enormity of what’s happening,” said Aaronson. “If, in these days of long-prophesied revelation and wonders and terrors, your main worry is your Bitcoin wallet, then go somewhere else for rumors about whether or not ECDSA is broken or whatever. I don’t have what you’re looking for here.” Magazine: ‘Bunker mode’ won’t protect your crypto, critics say

items.titleTr: California warns of flooding as king tides peak over Thanksgiving
items.summaryTr: Parts of the Canadian province of British Columbia may also be affected by the storms, which come as millions of people travel for the holiday.
items.articleText: California warns of flooding as king tides peak over Thanksgiving - Published Coastal areas of California are bracing for potential flooding as king tides peak in the state during the US Thanksgiving holiday. Water levels across the US state's vast coastline could reach over 8ft (2.4 metres) in some areas on Wednesday and Thursday, according to the National Weather Service (NWS) - breaking records set just last month. The NWS has warned parts of California could face major coastal flooding, which is likely to be significant in low-lying areas. There have already been some reports of flooding. Meanwhile, storms are also forecast for the Pacific Northwest, including the Canadian province of British Columbia, and eastern parts of the US. Portions of a pier in northern California came crashing down into the ocean on Wednesday as high tides and strong waves battered the structure, video showed. Beachgoers have been advised to stay away from the water's edge as large waves could suddenly form. Such waves could be damaging to piers and jetties, and could capsize small vessels, the NWS warned. Flooding has already been reported in the San Francisco Bay Area. In San Diego, a high tide of 8 ft 11in was recorded on Wednesday morning local time - potentially breaking the record for highest tide measured in the area, which was just set late last month at 7.98ft. In Los Angeles, the tide on Wednesday was thought to be as high 8.19 - the record for the city that was set only weeks ago 27 October when parts of the California coast experienced flooding. Recently set high tide records were also broken in Santa Barbara and La Jolla, according to preliminary data. King tides are the highest predicted tide of the year and are above the highest water level reached at high tide on an average day. While they typically occur once or twice a year in most coastal areas, they are happening more frequently in some as sea levels rise. These king tides are being strengthened by the strongest El Niño weather pattern on record. Storm systems are also expected to impact the US through the Thanksgiving holiday - one affecting the Pacific Northwest and another the eastern part of the country, the US National Weather Service said. On the east coast, a developing Nor'easter storm is expected to bring heavy rain, strong winds, and coastal flooding. Major impacts are expected to begin on Wednesday across the southeast, and move northward Wednesday night and on Thursday, the NWS said. "Those along the eastern seaboard can expect gusty, possibly damaging winds, heavy rain, and major coastal and marine impacts," it added. The developing storm system could bring about one to four inches rain along America's east coast and a peak of four to six inches in coastal North Carolina. The US department store chain Macy's has postponed its 100th annual Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York, which was due to take place on Thursday, until Saturday because of severe weather - the first time this has happened. The stormy weather on both coasts could disrupt travel for millions of people. The American Automobile Association (AAA) has predicted that 81.5 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles (80km) from home for Thanksgiving between Tuesday 24 November and Monday 30 November. Officials have also issued a flood warning along Vancouver's coastline in Canada's most western province of British Columbia. Residents were urged to take "immediate action to protect life and property", a weather warning from Environment and Climate Change Canada said. King tides were expected to potentially increase already high water levels there too. Related topics - Published12 October

items.title: The US pastor who wants to see women's right to vote overturned
items.summary: The movement to repeal women's right to vote has gained traction amongst some very conservative Christians.

items.titleTr: The US pastor who wants to see women's right to vote overturned
items.summaryTr: The movement to repeal women's right to vote has gained traction amongst some very conservative Christians.
items.articleText: The US pastor who wants to see women's right to vote overturned - Published "Patriarchy is in accordance with the way God made the world." That is the view of Pastor Doug Wilson, a conservative minister who the US Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth calls his mentor. Speaking to the BBC from his base in Moscow, Idaho, Wilson explained his view that a society led by men is "a very great blessing". It's a perspective Christians who disagree with him say is based on a fundamentalist understanding of the Bible, which promotes the subjugation of women. A self-described Christian nationalist, Wilson believes the US should be a theocracy, with gay sex criminalised, abortion outlawed, and people of other faiths unable to hold public office. In the past he has delivered a sermon on "The Lost Virtue of Sexism," arguing that the Bible says women should be excluded from leadership of the church, and certain roles in civic affairs. And as part of his views on the division between the sexes, he would like the 19th Amendment of the US constitution, which granted women the right to vote, to be repealed, something his detractors say is anti-democratic. The vast majority of Christians support women's right to vote, and dismiss his message as misogynistic and extreme. Rev. Canon Dana Colley Corsello, the vicar at the Washington National Cathedral, rejects Wilson's understanding of what the Bible says about women's roles. "In my mind, there is no biblical precedent or standing for what [Wilson has] proposed," she told the BBC. "I'm married, I have a husband, I have children. My husband and I are complete equals in everything we do." But while Wilson still represents a fringe perspective amongst Christians in the US, some of his views have been gaining support. The denomination he co-founded, the Communion of Reformed Evangelical Churches (CREC), has around 150 churches in the US. It's a drop in the ocean compared to the 350,000 or so other Christian congregations the US. But Wilson says membership continues to rise. His influence has grown in part because of his connection to Pete Hegseth. The Secretary of Defence is a "proud member" of a CREC affiliated church, a Pentagon spokesperson told the BBC, adding that the "secretary very much appreciates many of Mr. Wilson's writings and teachings". Wilson says the two have "a warm relationship", although he stresses it is "largely a pastoral one, not a political one". Wilson has led prayer services at the Pentagon, including one in mid-November. Joining Wilson on stage, Pete Hegseth said "thank you for your leadership, for your mentorship, for the things you've started, the truth you've told, your willingness to be bold." Hegseth worships at the Washington, DC branch of Wilson's network of churches. And there are other members of the current administration that worship there too, according to Wilson. Of all his views, it is his statements on women's suffrage that have garnered the most headlines. Wilson favours "household voting", where the head of the home – usually a man – votes on behalf of their family. It's the system used for elections within his church, although the women in Wilson's family do vote in civic elections in order to counter votes of liberals, he says. He says only in "odd" circumstances, such as divorce or bereavement or "where the husband was a quadriplegic," should women assume the role of head of household. Just 7% of votes in Wilson's church polity are cast by women. When challenged by the BBC, he admitted it was a system that gave men "outsized influence". Wilson says that repealing the 19th Amendment is "low" on the list of priorities for him and his congregation. But, he adds, "we do think it". 'Chipping away' at women's rights Julie Ingersoll, a professor of religious studies at the University of North Florida, says Wilson's beliefs are misogynistic and extreme - part of a world view that says women should be in complete submission to men in every part of their lives. It is extremely unlikely that the 19th Amendment would be repealed - it would require either a proposal from two-thirds of the House and Senate or two-thirds of the state legislatures. Three quarters of states would then need to ratify it. Still, says Ingersoll, the threat to women's rights should be taken seriously. "It's not unlike the battle that they waged against Roe versus Wade," she says, referencing the Supreme Court decision that granted women the right to an abortion. It was overturned in 2022, after years of legal battles that restricted women's access to abortion. "Thirty years ago, people would have said, oh, they're not gonna undo abortion rights. "But they chipped away and they kept chipping away until they were able to overturn it. And I see this as directly parallel." While Wilson says overturning the 19th Amendment could take a century or more, there are conservative Christians who are pushing for women to have their right to vote removed more immediately. A Christian manosphere? Last February, pastor Dale Partridge posted on Instagram saying "We will repeal the 19th Amendment within ten years". Partridge, who has around 900k followers across social media, credits Wilson as being someone who "broke the ice" for "strong politics and theology". Partridge has said that "the majority of women are not capable of responsible voting" because too many of them are liberal. He also frequently collaborates on podcasts with another conservative pastor named Joel Webbon. Webbon, whose New Christian Right YouTube channel has more than 190k subscribers, has said that women's "desires are wicked". The solution, he claims, is to "take away women's vote". He was once friendly with Wilson, although they have since fallen out. "Those guys have overshot by a long way," says Wilson of the two younger pastors. "They are disruptors and basically rage baiting." So what might be driving those who support the effort? Kelly Marino, an associate professor at Sacred Heart University who studies women's suffrage, says that the last decade has seen big wins for the women's rights movement, and "liberal political ideology" in general. But, she argues, "any time where there was sort of this peak of feminism, there've been people who respond aggressively and try to push back". Added to that are the high levels of uncertainty and conflict that have characterised the post-Covid period. "I think there's been this craving for tradition and things that felt safe," Marino says. That, she says, can be seen in the popularity of notions such as being a "tradwife" or "soft girl", who reject career goals in favour of traditionally female roles of wife and mother. Marino says that while she doesn't think the constitution could be changed in the immediate future, the conversation around repealing the 19th Amendment is shaping the way people think about women's roles in general. Global expansion Canon Corsello, the Vicar at Washington Cathedral, sees the midterm election results as a repudiation of the push against women's rights. "Cultural issues did not translate in this election", she says. "When people are preaching love, empathy, inclusion... that actually resonated with people". Wilson's views have, however, been gaining ground beyond the US. The CREC has more than 30 churches internationally, including in Poland, Japan and Brazil. The latter country has seen its own movement of right-wing influencers pressing for the removal of women's suffrage, with some leaning on religious language to make their point. Wilson wants to continue expanding his brand of Christianity around the world, and has recently accepted a church in England into his network. While CREC churches in each country have their own distinct characteristics, Wilson says their core beliefs are the same. When it comes to the US, he says his ideal scenario would be for his congregations to "to practice what we believe in the church and for outsiders to look at that and envy it and say, man, that seems like a good system". Global expansion Canon Corsello, the Vicar at Washington Cathedral, sees the midterm election results as a repudiation of the push against women's rights. "Cultural issues did not translate in this election", she says. "When people are preaching love, empathy, inclusion... that actually resonated with people". Wilson's views have, however, been gaining ground beyond the US. The CREC has more than 30 churches internationally, including in Poland, Japan and Brazil. The latter country has seen its own movement of right-wing influencers pressing for the removal of women's suffrage, with some leaning on religious language to make their point. Wilson wants to continue expanding his brand of Christianity around the world, and has recently accepted a church in England into his network. While CREC churches in each country have their own distinct characteristics, Wilson says their core beliefs are the same. When it comes to the US, he says his ideal scenario would be for his congregations to "to practice what we believe in the church and for outsiders to look at that and envy it and say, man, that seems like a good system". items.summary: After eight years of Socialist-led rule, snap elections are taking place on Sunday with conservative Alberto Núñez Feijóo vying to win office.

items.titleTr: Spanish elections: What you need to know and what's at stake
items.summaryTr: After eight years of Socialist-led rule, snap elections are taking place on Sunday with conservative Alberto Núñez Feijóo vying to win office.
items.articleText: Spanish elections: What you need to know and what's at stake - Published After eight years of Socialist-led government under Pedro Sánchez, Spain is at a crossroads. Snap elections are taking place on Sunday 29 November, and voters face a choice of continued left-wing rule or a conservative-led government, with the likely support of far-right Vox. Who is favourite to win? Alberto Núñez Feijóo's conservative People's Party is narrowly ahead of the Socialist PSOE in most polls. He has spoken of Spain being probably at "the most significant moment in our country for the past 50 years", and he aims to "repair the state, regenerate democracy, reunited the nation and recover Spain's ambition and self-esteem". But it is unlikely he could do anything without the backing of Vox, who are third in the opinion polls. For more on Feijóo and who else to watch in this election - read here. Spain has a population of almost 50 million, and almost 39 million people have the right to vote for the Congress and the upper house, the Senate. The polls open at 09:00 (08:00 GMT) on Sunday and close at 20:00 (19:00 GMT), when the first exit polls come out. Why are there snap elections? Sánchez called this vote eight months early after MPs rejected planned changes to Spain's housing laws. He was responding to nationwide protests after an 87-year-old woman called Maricarmen Abascal was evicted from her rented flat in Madrid and later died. But his government lost the support of a centre-right party called Junts from the north-eastern region of Catalonia which sought to protect the rights of property owners. Housing remains one of the hot-button issues for voters, but they are also focused on the high cost of living, corruption and immigration. Why housing is so important Spain's property prices and rents have soared by more than 80% from 2015 to 2025, and wages have not kept pace. Spain has a combination of high demand and scarce supply: the Bank of Spain estimates 700,000 homes are needed to ease the pressure. The result is that millions of Spaniards have little chance to buy a house, while they live in fear of eviction if their rent is increased. On 11 November, four million Spaniards were galvanised into joining the first general strike since 2012, according to the unions. Pedro Sánchez has embraced housing reform as a big campaign issue and left-wing parties have promised rent controls and protection against eviction, while the right is focusing on building more homes, tax breaks for homebuyers and planning deregulation. Does Sánchez have a chance of retaining power? Support for the Socialists is down from 2023, but even then he came second in the race and relied on the backing of other parties, mainly on the left, to stay in power. This time those other left-wing parties, in particular the Broad Front (Frente Amplio) have fallen back and the big questions now are more about Feijóo's conservatives. "It is a demobilisation of the left. Sanchez's party is not doing well," says Jacobo Ramos Folch, Policy Analyst and visiting professor at the University of Navarra. "That lack of majority is really a reality – and the rise of Vox. What is changing that shift of majorities is the rise of Vox." Who are Vox and what do they stand for? Vox have been around since 2013 but polls suggest this time they could almost double their 33 seats in Spain's lower house, the Congress. Their big themes are "national priority" – putting Spanish citizens first for subsidies and welfare, along with repatriating migrants "in an illegal situation" and "remigration" of foreigners who do not contribute to Spain. Migration another key election issue Migration has become a key challenge for Spain, and Alberto Nuñez Feijoo has accused his rival of being a "problem for Europe when it comes to immigration" after the influx of tens of thousands of migrants into the exclave of Ceuta from neighbouring Morocco in July. This month too, the Canary Island of El Hierro has seen record arrivals, with 2,000 people landing there on 24 November. Abascal has spoken of "another invasion". And yet a recent CIS survey put it far behind housing, cost of living, healthcare and working conditions. The PP and Vox have bitterly criticised the Socialist-led government for a drive to legalise unauthorised migrants this year that attracted 1.2 million applications. Feijóo's party wants to see more controlled immigration. Vox has called for mass deportations. - Clashing political visions reflect a divided Spain ahead of election - Published1 day ago How corruption has hit Sánchez's government Feijóo has accused the Socialists of being "the most corrupt party" that Spain had ever seen, and a number of cases have involved Sánchez's inner circle and family. People should distinguish between real and "fictitious" corruption allegations, says el momento más trascendental. His former transport minister José Luis Ábalos has been given 24 years in prison over multiple corruption offences. Leading party figure Santos Cerdán awaits trial for alleged bribery and denies wrongdoing. Sánchez's wife Begoña Gómez faces trial for alleged misuse of public funds and using her marriage to further her academic career. She denies wrongdoing. And his brother David Sánchez has been banned from public office for nine years for administrative misconduct. Will the conservatives go into coalition with Vox? Feijóo has made clear his objective is to form a majority and make "parliamentary support agreements" with Vox. As far as a coalition is concerned, he says he will respect the will of Spanish voters, but maintains Abascal has never talked to him about running any ministries. The PP leader is clear that Vox's national priority policy would run counter to Spain's constitution and European Union treaties: "No-one can sign illegal agreements." Even if they were to go into coalition, Camino Mortera-Martinez of the Centre for European Reform, and a former European affairs adviser to the Spanish prime minister is not convinced Vox would wield much influence. "They're not going to get any of the core ministries. They're not going to get defence or home affairs or foreign policy or economy," she told the BBC. Even if they take over the education ministry, Mortera-Martinez argues education policy is largely devolved to Spain's regional governments. What is Vox's record so far? Since 2022, Vox has worked with the PP in a series of regional coalition governments, holding ministries such as culture and tourism. At the time Feijóo had reservations about Vox joining the conservatives in government in Castilla y León. The following year they went into coalition with the conservatives in Valencia, Aragón, Murcia, and Extremadura, but pulled out of all five governments in 2024 when they refused to accept unaccompanied migrant children being moved to their regions. They have since signed new coalition pacts with the PP in Extremadura, Aragón, Castilla y León and Andalusia. Why are regions important in Spanish politics? Unlike many European countries Spain has 17 autonomous communities (and two cities) that have their own parliament and their own powers. Catalonia in the north-east and the Basque Country in the north have their own police forces. The regions matter to Sunday's result. Catalonia alone has 48 seats out of the 350 in Spain's parliament, and the Socialists have recently come to rely on regional parties for support. Sánchez's government relied on the support of Basque separatists Bildu and two Catalan parties, ERC on the left and Junts on the right. But when Junts refused to back his housing reform, he decided to dissolve parliament. How the election system works Spain is made up of 50 constituencies which each have a minimum of two seats. The exclaves of Ceuta and Melilla both have one, and the other 248 seats are divided proportionally according to voter numbers. Madrid province will have 38 seats, Barcelona 32 and Valencia 16. To win a seat, a party has to win 3% of the vote in a province, but in smaller provinces with fewer seats parties generally need more than that.

items.titleTr: Pasifik GYO (PSGYO) paylarında 71 milyon TL'lik SPK cezası: 8 ayrı yaptırım kararı
items.summaryTr: SPK, Pasifik GYO paylarının borsada satışında pay satış bilgi formu yükümlülüğünün dolanıldığı gerekçesiyle 8 ayrı yaptırım kaydı kapsamında toplam 71 milyon 26 bin TL idari para cezası uygulanmasına karar verdi. Ceza tutarı kişi ve kuruluş başına 8,87 milyon TL oldu.
items.articleText: Pasifik GYO (PSGYO) paylarında 71 milyon TL'lik SPK cezası: 8 ayrı yaptırım kararı - SPK, Pasifik GYO paylarının borsada satışında pay satış bilgi formu yükümlülüğünün dolanıldığı gerekçesiyle 8 ayrı yaptırım kaydı kapsamında toplam 71 milyon 26 bin TL idari para cezası uygulanmasına karar verdi. Ceza tutarı kişi ve kuruluş başına 8,87 milyon TL oldu. Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK), Pasifik Gayrimenkul Yatırım Ortaklığı (PSGYO) pay piyasasında gerçekleştirilen işlemlere yönelik incelemesini tamamladı. Kurul, şirket paylarının borsada satışa konu edilmesi sırasında pay satış bilgi formu hazırlama ve SPK tarafından onaylanan formu ilan etme yükümlülüğünün dolanıldığı gerekçesiyle 8 ayrı yaptırım kaydı kapsamında toplam 71 milyon 26 bin 384 TL idari para cezası uygulanmasına karar verdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle SPK'nın 25 Kasım 2026 tarihli 2026/85 sayılı bülteninde yer alan karara göre, yaptırım uygulanan kişi ve kuruluşların her biri için ceza tutarı 8 milyon 878 bin 298,07 TL olarak belirlendi. Pasifik GYO dosyasında kimlere ceza verildi? SPK'nın kararında Mehmet Erdoğan, Fatih Erdoğan ve Abdulkerim Fırat'ın yanı sıra Bulls Yatırım Menkul Değerler AŞ, Bulls Portföy Yönetimi AŞ, Pusula Portföy Yönetimi AŞ ve Pardus Portföy Yönetimi AŞ'nin adı yer aldı. Kurulun tablosunda Pusula Portföy Yönetimi AŞ, farklı fonlar üzerinden gerçekleştirilen işlemler nedeniyle iki ayrı yaptırım kaydında bulunuyor. Böylece toplam sekiz ayrı ceza kaydı oluşuyor. SPK'nın tespit ettiği ihlal ne? Kurulun kararında, Pasifik GYO paylarının borsada satışa konu edilmesi öncesinde hazırlanması ve SPK tarafından onaylanarak ilan edilmesi gereken pay satış bilgi formuna ilişkin yükümlülüğün dolanıldığı belirtildi. İhlalin, VII-128.1 sayılı Pay Tebliği'nin 27'nci maddesi, VI-104.1 sayılı Piyasa Bozucu Eylemler Tebliği'nin 7'nci maddesinin üçüncü fıkrası ve SPK Kurul Karar Organı'nın 14 Şubat 2023 tarihli ilke kararı kapsamında değerlendirildiği bildirildi. SPK bülteninde KUYAS, SMRVA ve SVGYO kararları da var SPK'nın aynı bültende açıkladığı diğer yaptırımlar arasında Kuyaş Yatırım (KUYAS), Sümer Varlık Yönetim (SMRVA) ve Savur Gayrimenkul Yatırım Ortaklığı (SVGYO) pay piyasalarındaki işlemlere ilişkin kararlar da bulunuyor. KUYAS pay piyasasında gerçekleştirilen işlemler nedeniyle 12 kişi hakkında suç duyurusunda bulunulmasına ve bu kişilere 2 yıl süreyle borsalarda işlem yasağı uygulanmasına karar verildi. SMRVA pay piyasasına ilişkin incelemede 41 kişi hakkında suç duyurusu kararı alınırken, ilgili kişiler için 2 yıllık işlem yasağı getirildi. Tera Yatırım Bankası ve Tera Portföy Yönetimi'nin kendi nam ve hesaplarına SMRVA pay piyasasında işlem yapması da aynı süreyle yasaklandı. SVGYO pay piyasasında gerçekleştirilen işlemler nedeniyle 38 kişi hakkında suç duyurusunda bulunulmasına ve 2 yıl işlem yasağı uygulanmasına karar verildi. Pardus Portföy, Tera Portföy ve Tera Yatırım Bankası için de SVGYO paylarıyla sınırlı işlem kısıtlamaları getirildi. İlgili kişilerin lisansları da iptal edildi SPK, KUYAS, SMRVA ve SVGYO pay piyasalarındaki işlemler nedeniyle haklarında suç duyurusunda bulunulan ve bültende isimleri belirtilen kişilerin sahip oldukları tüm sermaye piyasası lisanslarının işlem yasağı süresince iptal edilmesine karar verdi. Öte yandan İhlas Ev Aletleri (IHEVA) pay piyasasındaki işlemler nedeniyle İhsan Uzunyol, İlyas Meydan ve Derya Uzunyol hakkında 6 ay süreyle geçici işlem yasağı uygulanması kararlaştırıldı. SPK'nın suç duyurusu kararları, ilgili kişiler hakkında kesinleşmiş mahkûmiyet anlamına gelmiyor. İdari yaptırımlar ve işlem yasakları ise Kurulun açıkladığı kararlar kapsamında uygulanacak.

items.articleText: Resmi Gazete'de duyuruldu: İki ülkeden ithal edilen bebek ürünlerine 5 yıl daha ek vergi - Ticaret Bakanlığı, Çin ve Tayland menşeli plastik bebek beslenme ve bakım ürünlerine uygulanan dampinge karşı vergileri 5 yıl daha uzattı. Çin'den ithal edilen ürünlere yüzde 12, Tayland'dan gelenlere yüzde 26 ek vergi uygulanacak. Ticaret Bakanlığı, Çin Halk Cumhuriyeti ve Tayland Krallığı menşeli plastik bebek beslenme, emzirme ve bakım ürünlerine yönelik dampinge karşı kesin önlemin devamına karar verdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle 26 Kasım 2026 tarihli Resmî Gazete'de yayımlanan 2026/33 sayılı Tebliğ kapsamında, söz konusu ürünlerin ithalatında uygulanan ek vergiler 5 yıl daha yürürlükte kalacak. Çin'den gelen ürünlere yüzde 12, Tayland'a yüzde 26 vergi Yeni düzenlemeyle birlikte ülkelere göre uygulanacak dampinge karşı önlem oranları şöyle belirlendi: Vergiler, ürünlerin CIF bedeli üzerinden hesaplanacak. CIF bedeli, eşyanın maliyet, sigorta ve navlun dâhil değerini ifade ediyor. Hangi ürünler ek vergi kapsamında? Düzenleme, plastikten üretilen bebek beslenme, emzirme ve bakım ürünlerini kapsıyor. Vergi uygulanacak ürünler arasında şunlar bulunuyor: - Emzik, biberon ve biberon emziği - Mama kapları, mama kaşıkları ve çatal-kaşık setleri - Alıştırma bardakları ve bardak uçları - Süt saklama poşetleri ve kapları - Diş kaşıyıcıları ve emzik askıları - Manuel burun aspiratörleri ve burun temizleyiciler - Göğüs koruyucular ve manuel göğüs pompaları - Emzik ve çatal-kaşık saklama kutuları Önlem 5 yıl boyunca uygulanacak Ticaret Bakanlığı tarafından yürütülen nihai gözden geçirme soruşturmasında, mevcut önlemin kaldırılması halinde damping ve zararın devam etmesinin veya yeniden meydana gelmesinin muhtemel olduğu sonucuna ulaşıldı. Bu değerlendirme doğrultusunda, mevcut dampinge karşı önlemin devam etmesine karar verildi. Tebliğ, yayımlandığı 26 Kasım 2026 tarihinde yürürlüğe girdi. Düzenleme kapsamındaki önlem, yürürlük tarihinden itibaren 5 yıl sonra sona erecek. Ancak bu tarihten önce yeni bir nihai gözden geçirme soruşturması başlatılması halinde önlem, soruşturma sonuçlanıncaya kadar uygulanmaya devam edecek.

Çin'den ithal edilen ürünlere yüzde 12, Tayland'dan gelenlere yüzde 26 ek vergi uygulanacak. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle 26 Kasım 2026 tarihli Resmî Gazete'de yayımlanan 2026/33 sayılı Tebliğ kapsamında, söz konusu ürünlerin ithalatında uygulanan ek vergiler 5 yıl daha yürürlükte kalacak. Çin'den gelen ürünlere yüzde 12, Tayland'a yüzde 26 vergi Yeni düzenlemeyle birlikte ülkelere göre uygulanacak dampinge karşı önlem oranları şöyle belirlendi: Vergiler, ürünlerin CIF bedeli üzerinden hesaplanacak. CIF bedeli, eşyanın maliyet, sigorta ve navlun dâhil değerini ifade ediyor. Hangi ürünler ek vergi kapsamında? Düzenleme, plastikten üretilen bebek beslenme, emzirme ve bakım ürünlerini kapsıyor. Vergi uygulanacak ürünler arasında şunlar bulunuyor: - Emzik, biberon ve biberon emziği - Mama kapları, mama kaşıkları ve çatal-kaşık setleri - Alıştırma bardakları ve bardak uçları - Süt saklama poşetleri ve kapları - Diş kaşıyıcıları ve emzik askıları - Manuel burun aspiratörleri ve burun temizleyiciler - Göğüs koruyucular ve manuel göğüs pompaları - Emzik ve çatal-kaşık saklama kutuları Önlem 5 yıl boyunca uygulanacak Ticaret Bakanlığı tarafından yürütülen nihai gözden geçirme soruşturmasında, mevcut önlemin kaldırılması halinde damping ve zararın devam etmesinin veya yeniden meydana gelmesinin muhtemel olduğu sonucuna ulaşıldı. Bu değerlendirme doğrultusunda, mevcut dampinge karşı önlemin devam etmesine karar verildi. Tebliğ, yayımlandığı 26 Kasım 2026 tarihinde yürürlüğe girdi. Düzenleme kapsamındaki önlem, yürürlük tarihinden itibaren 5 yıl sonra sona erecek. Ancak bu tarihten önce yeni bir nihai gözden geçirme soruşturması başlatılması halinde önlem, soruşturma sonuçlanıncaya kadar uygulanmaya devam edecek.

items.titleTr: Trump'ın Nvidia hayranlığı... 44 alım satımda milyonlarca dolarlık hareket
items.summaryTr: ABD Başkanı Donald Trump'ın yatırım hesapları, ocak-eylül döneminde Nvidia hisselerinde en az 44 işlem gerçekleştirdi. Finansal beyanlara göre milyonlarca dolarlık alım ve satım yapan portföylerin toplam işlem değerinin kesin tutarı açıklanmadı.
items.articleText: Trump'ın Nvidia hayranlığı... 44 alım satımda milyonlarca dolarlık hareket - ABD Başkanı Donald Trump'ın yatırım hesapları, ocak-eylül döneminde Nvidia hisselerinde en az 44 işlem gerçekleştirdi. Finansal beyanlara göre milyonlarca dolarlık alım ve satım yapan portföylerin toplam işlem değerinin kesin tutarı açıklanmadı. ABD Başkanı Donald Trump'ın yatırım hesaplarının, dünyanın en büyük çip üreticilerinden Nvidia'nın hisselerinde yılın ilk dokuz ayında en az 44 kez alım ve satım yaptığı ortaya çıktı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle BBC'nin Trump'ın mali beyanlarını inceleyerek hazırladığı analize göre, ocak-eylül döneminde Trump'ın yatırım hesapları 5,2 milyon ila 17 milyon dolar değerinde Nvidia hissesi satın aldı. Aynı dönemde 4,4 milyon ila 12 milyon dolar değerinde hisse satışı gerçekleştirildi. ABD Hükümet Etik Ofisi'ne sunulan mali beyanlarda işlem tutarlarının kesin rakamlar yerine alt ve üst sınırlar halinde bildirilmesi nedeniyle alım satımların toplam değeri net olarak hesaplanamıyor. Trump'ın portföyünde yıl sonunda 58 milyon dolara kadar Nvidia hissesi vardı Trump'ın yatırım portföylerinde 2025 yılı sonunda 12,5 milyon ila 58 milyon dolar değerinde Nvidia hissesi bulunuyordu. Açıklanan işlemler, Trump'ın Nvidia'daki diğer yatırım ürünlerini kapsamıyor. Ayrıca mali beyanlar, şirketin son dönemdeki gelişmelerini ve hisse fiyatındaki dalgalanmaları da içermiyor. Beyaz Saray: Yatırımları bağımsız üçüncü taraflar yönetiyor Beyaz Saray, Trump'ın hisse senedi ve tahvil portföylerinin bağımsız üçüncü taraflar tarafından yönetildiğini açıkladı. Yapılan açıklamada, Trump'ın ve ailesinin yatırımların nasıl değerlendirileceği veya alım satım işlemlerinin ne zaman gerçekleştirileceği konusunda yönlendirme yapma, işlemleri etkileme ya da görüş bildirme imkânının bulunmadığı belirtildi. Trump'ın yatırımlardan kazancı 2,2 milyar doları aştı Trump'ın ikinci başkanlık döneminin ilk yılına ilişkin mali beyan raporuna göre ABD Başkanı, çeşitli yatırımları ve ticari faaliyetlerinden en az 2,2 milyar dolar kazanç elde etti. Nvidia, yapay zekâ sektöründeki büyümenin etkisiyle dünyanın en değerli şirketleri arasında yer alıyor. Finansal hizmetler şirketi State Street'e göre Nvidia, S&P 500 endeksinin yüzde 6'sından fazlasını oluşturuyor ve Apple'ın ardından endeksin en büyük ikinci şirketi konumunda bulunuyor. Trump'ın yatırım hesaplarında Apple hisseleri de sıklıkla alınıp satılıyor. Trump, Nvidia CEO'sunun görevine dönüşünde rol oynadığını söyledi Nvidia'nın kurucu ortağı ve CEO'su Jensen Huang'ın görevine dönüş süreci de Trump'ın şirketle ilişkisine yönelik tartışmaları gündeme taşıdı. Trump, ABD medyasına yaptığı açıklamada Huang'ın görevine dönmesi için şirketin yönetim kurulunu ikna ettiğini ve bu konuda "anlaşmayı kendisinin yaptığını" söyledi. Nvidia yönetim kurulu ise ABD hükümetinin üst düzey yetkililerinden Huang'ın ulusal güvenlik açısından risk oluşturmadığı yönünde görüş aldığını bildirdi. Nvidia'nın Çin'e çip ihracatı da tartışılıyor Huang'ın yeniden göreve getirilmesi ve Trump'ın süreçteki rolü, ABD'de Cumhuriyetçi ve Demokrat siyasetçiler arasında endişelere yol açtı. Tartışmaların diğer başlığını ise Nvidia'nın gelişmiş bilgisayar çiplerinin Çin'e ihracatı oluşturuyor. Şirketin ABD'nin Çin'e yönelik ihracat kısıtlamalarına uyumu da gündemdeki yerini koruyor. Virginia Üniversitesi'ne bağlı Miller Center'dan başkanlık tarihçisi Barbara Perry, BBC'ye yaptığı değerlendirmede Trump'ın yatırımları ile başkanlık görevi arasındaki ilişkiyi "Başkanlık tarihinde daha önce gördüğümüz hiçbir şeye benzemiyor" sözleriyle değerlendirdi.

items.titleTr: Altın yatırımcısı tetikte: Sert çöküş 15 ayın dibine geldi! Fed ve faiz korkusu büyüyor
items.summaryTr: ABD'de enflasyonun hızlanması ve Fed'in aralık ayında faiz artıracağı beklentisi altın fiyatlarını baskıladı. Ons altın 2025 Ağustos'tan bu yana en düşük seviyeye gerilerken, gün içinde 3.500 doların da altına indi.
items.articleText: Altın yatırımcısı tetikte: Sert çöküş 15 ayın dibine geldi! Fed ve faiz korkusu büyüyor ABD'de enflasyonun hızlanması ve Fed'in aralık ayında faiz artıracağı beklentisi altın fiyatlarını baskıladı. Ons altın 2025 Ağustos'tan bu yana en düşük seviyeye gerilerken, gün içinde 3.500 doların da altına indi. Altın bir yıldan uzun sürenin dibinde Altın fiyatları, ABD'de açıklanan güçlü enflasyon verilerinin ardından bir yılı aşkın sürenin en düşük seviyelerine geriledi. Ons altın gün içinde 3.500 doların altını gördü. Ons altın 3.547 dolara geriledi Spot altın, gün içinde kayıplarının bir bölümünü telafi etse de yüzde 0,2 düşüşle ons başına 3.547,29 dolardan işlem gördü. Altın, seansın erken saatlerinde Ağustos 2025'ten bu yana en düşük seviyesini test etti. ABD enflasyonu altını baskıladı ABD'de Fed'in yakından takip ettiği Kişisel Tüketim Harcamaları (PCE) fiyat endeksi ekim ayında aylık yüzde 0,3 arttı. Endeks, eylül ayında yüzde 0,5 yükselmişti. Enflasyonun Fed'in yüzde 2'lik hedefinin üzerinde kalması, faiz indirimi beklentilerini zayıflatırken altın üzerindeki baskıyı artırdı. Piyasa Fed'in faiz artışını fiyatlıyor CME FedWatch verilerine göre piyasalar, Fed'in aralık ayındaki toplantısında faiz artırmasını tamamen fiyatlamış durumda. Fed son faiz artışını eylül ayında gerçekleştirmişti. Yüksek faiz oranları, faiz getirisi bulunmayan altının yatırımcılar açısından cazibesini azaltıyor. Altın rekor seviyesinden yüzde 37 geriledi Reuters'ın aktardığı verilere göre spot altın fiyatları, yılın başlarında gördüğü rekor seviyeden bu yana yaklaşık yüzde 37 değer kaybetti. Faiz beklentileri ve güçlü enflasyon verileri, değerli metaldeki düşüşü derinleştiren başlıca unsurlar arasında yer aldı. Gümüş ve platin de geriledi Diğer değerli metallerde de düşüş görüldü. Spot gümüş yüzde 0,5 kayıpla 40,68 dolara geriledi ve gün içinde Ağustos 2025'ten bu yana en düşük seviyesini gördü. Platin yüzde 0,7 düşüşle 1.266,58 dolara inerken, gün içinde Haziran 2025'ten bu yana en düşük seviyesine geriledi. Paladyumda sınırlı yükseliş Değerli metallerdeki genel düşüş eğiliminin aksine paladyum yüzde 0,8 yükselerek ons başına 860,22 dolara çıktı. Ancak paladyum da günün erken saatlerinde 2017'den bu yana en düşük seviyesini test etti. Trump'ın yeni tarife hamlesi piyasaları sarstı ABD Başkanı Donald Trump, Çin dahil büyük ticaret ortaklarına yönelik yeni gümrük tarifeleri önererek küresel ticaret gerilimini yeniden artırdı. Yeni tarife önerileri, teknoloji hisselerindeki satışlarla birlikte piyasalardaki baskıyı derinleştirdi. Wall Street'te teknoloji hisseleri satışta Altın fiyatlarındaki düşüşle aynı dönemde ABD borsalarında da sert satışlar yaşandı. Teknoloji ağırlıklı Nasdaq endeksi yüzde 4 geriledi. Yapay zeka bağlantılı hisselerdeki satışlar ve yapay zeka yatırımlarının beklenen getiriyi sağlayıp sağlayamayacağına ilişkin endişeler piyasalardaki risk iştahını zayıflattı.

Fed son faiz artışını eylül ayında gerçekleştirmişti. Yüksek faiz oranları, faiz getirisi bulunmayan altının yatırımcılar açısından cazibesini azaltıyor. Altın rekor seviyesinden yüzde 37 geriledi Reuters'ın aktardığı verilere göre spot altın fiyatları, yılın başlarında gördüğü rekor seviyeden bu yana yaklaşık yüzde 37 değer kaybetti. Faiz beklentileri ve güçlü enflasyon verileri, değerli metaldeki düşüşü derinleştiren başlıca unsurlar arasında yer aldı. Gümüş ve platin de geriledi Diğer değerli metallerde de düşüş görüldü. Spot gümüş yüzde 0,5 kayıpla 40,68 dolara geriledi ve gün içinde Ağustos 2025'ten bu yana en düşük seviyesini gördü. Platin yüzde 0,7 düşüşle 1.266,58 dolara inerken, gün içinde Haziran 2025'ten bu yana en düşük seviyesine geriledi. Paladyumda sınırlı yükseliş Değerli metallerdeki genel düşüş eğiliminin aksine paladyum yüzde 0,8 yükselerek ons başına 860,22 dolara çıktı. Ancak paladyum da günün erken saatlerinde 2017'den bu yana en düşük seviyesini test etti. Trump'ın yeni tarife hamlesi piyasaları sarstı ABD Başkanı Donald Trump, Çin dahil büyük ticaret ortaklarına yönelik yeni gümrük tarifeleri önererek küresel ticaret gerilimini yeniden artırdı. Yeni tarife önerileri, teknoloji hisselerindeki satışlarla birlikte piyasalardaki baskıyı derinleştirdi. Wall Street'te teknoloji hisseleri satışta Altın fiyatlarındaki düşüşle aynı dönemde ABD borsalarında da sert satışlar yaşandı. Teknoloji ağırlıklı Nasdaq endeksi yüzde 4 geriledi. Yapay zeka bağlantılı hisselerdeki satışlar ve yapay zeka yatırımlarının beklenen getiriyi sağlayıp sağlayamayacağına ilişkin endişeler piyasalardaki risk iştahını zayıflattı.

items.summaryTr: Fed'in Beige Book raporuna göre ABD ekonomisi son haftalarda ılımlı büyümesini sürdürürken enflasyon yüksek seyrini korudu. Enerji, taşımacılık ve sağlık maliyetlerindeki artış şirketler üzerindeki baskıyı artırdı.
items.articleText: Fed çarpıcı raporu yayımladı: Faiz kararı öncesi piyasalar için kötü sinyal - Fed'in Beige Book raporuna göre ABD ekonomisi son haftalarda ılımlı büyümesini sürdürürken enflasyon yüksek seyrini korudu. Enerji, taşımacılık ve sağlık maliyetlerindeki artış şirketler üzerindeki baskıyı artırdı. ABD Merkez Bankası'nın (Fed) son ekonomik değerlendirme raporu, ülkede büyümenin devam ettiğini ancak enflasyon baskılarının henüz hafiflemediğini ortaya koydu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Fed'in çarşamba günü yayımladığı Beige Book raporuna göre, ABD'nin büyük bölümünde ekonomik faaliyet son haftalarda "hafif ila ılımlı" hızda büyüdü. İstihdam seviyeleri yükselirken fiyat artışları da önceki raporlama dönemine benzer şekilde ılımlı seyretti. Şirketlerin maliyet baskısı sürüyor Raporda, farklı sektörlerde faaliyet gösteren şirketlerin enerji, taşımacılık, sağlık, sigorta ve gümrük tarifelerinden kaynaklanan maliyet baskılarının devam ettiğini bildirdiği belirtildi. Girdi maliyetlerinin satış fiyatlarından daha hızlı arttığına dikkat çekilen raporda, rekabet baskısı ve müşterilerin fiyatlara duyarlılığının şirketlerin artan maliyetleri tamamen tüketicilere yansıtmasını engellediği ifade edildi. Şirketlerin önümüzdeki aylarda hem giderlerin hem de satış fiyatlarının yükselmeye devam etmesini beklediği aktarıldı. Fed'in faiz kararı öncesinde enflasyon endişesi Beige Book raporu, Fed'in 8-9 Aralık'taki para politikası toplantısı öncesinde yayımlandı. Fed'in politika faizi şu anda yüzde 3,75-4,00 aralığında bulunuyor. Piyasalarda Fed'in aralık toplantısında en az 25 baz puanlık faiz artışına gideceği beklentisi bulunurken, son dönemde hisse senedi piyasalarında yaşanan sert satışlar bu beklentileri bir miktar zayıflattı. Buna karşın Fed yetkilileri, beş yılı aşkın süredir yüzde 2'lik hedefin üzerinde seyreden ve son dönemde yeniden hızlanan enflasyona ilişkin endişelerini artırdı. PCE enflasyonu üç yılın zirvesine çıktı ABD Ticaret Bakanlığı'nın çarşamba günü açıkladığı verilere göre, Fed'in enflasyon hedeflemesinde dikkate aldığı Kişisel Tüketim Harcamaları (PCE) fiyat endeksi ekim ayında yıllık yüzde 3,8 yükseldi. Gıda ve enerji fiyatlarının hariç tutulduğu çekirdek PCE enflasyonu ise yıllık yüzde 3,3'e çıkarak beklentilerin üzerinde gerçekleşti. Bu oran, çekirdek enflasyonda son üç yılın en yüksek seviyesine işaret etti. Ara seçimlerin ardından yayımlanan ilk Beige Book Son Beige Book, ABD'de ara seçimlerin ardından ekonomiye ilişkin değerlendirmeleri içeren ilk rapor oldu. Enflasyon ve yaşam maliyeti endişelerinin öne çıktığı seçimlerde Demokratlar, Kongre'nin her iki kanadında da çoğunluğu kazandı. Reuters'ın aktardığına göre seçim sonuçları, Trump yönetiminin politikalarına yönelik güçlü bir tepki olarak değerlendirildi.

items.articleText: Borsada 2 şirketten temettü kararı: Şirketler kaç lira kar payı dağıtacak? YAYIN TARİHİ, 25 Kasım 2026 21:20 PAYLAŞ - Borsa İstanbul'da Bor Şeker hisse başına brüt 0,2604 TL, net 0,2213 TL temettü açıklarken Trabzon Liman İşletmeciliği kâr payı dağıtmama kararı aldı. Borsa İstanbul'da işlem gören iki şirket, 25 Kasım Çarşamba günü temettü kararlarını Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'na (KAP) bildirdi. Bor Şeker temettü dağıtma kararı alırken Trabzon Liman İşletmeciliği kâr payı dağıtmayacağını açıkladı. Bor Şeker temettü dağıtacak CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Bor Şeker A.Ş. (BORSK), hisse başına brüt 0,2604166 TL, net 0,2213541 TL temettü açıklaması yaptı. Şirketin genel kurul kararı kapsamında temettü ödemesinin 31 Aralık 2026'ya kadar gerçekleştirilmesi planlanıyor. Trabzon Liman temettü dağıtmayacak Trabzon Liman İşletmeciliği A.Ş. (TLMAN) ise genel kurul kararı doğrultusunda temettü dağıtmama kararı aldı. Şirketin açıkladığı karara göre hisse başına brüt ve net temettü ödemesi yapılmayacak.
